text:
maria: Hey SRE, getting multiple customer reports: p95 jumped from ~2.2s to 8-12s for requests served from Dedicated pool dp-42 since ~09:15 UTC. Several customers opened support tickets. Anyone seeing this in metrics? :wave:

kevin: saw the alert too. Autoscaler showed rapid scale-up events but nodes weren't serving for a while — warmup delay looks high. p99 spike at 09:16:12 UTC. Queues grew and token cost spiked.

james: digging into provisioner logs now. Noting GPU attach failures on several new nodes. Pasting snippet below.

james: ```
2026-03-15T09:16:03Z [provisioner] create node id=node-xyz status=PROVISIONING hw=gpu-v2
2026-03-15T09:16:06Z [driver] attach gpu failed err="nvml timeout" retry=1
2026-03-15T09:16:08Z [provisioner] node id=node-xyz warmup=0/1 ready=false
```

sandhya: That looks like cold GPU bootstrap (CUDA driver/nvidia modules) timing out during first attach. We saw something similar in canary last month when kernel-module compile took longer in certain AZs. Which image/kernel are these nodes using?

kevin: They launched from image inference-2026-02-28-gpu (kernel 6.1), and ops-bot shows a rolling update kicked off at 09:12 which might've coincided with traffic surge.

maria: Support thread INC-5432 has several customers reporting 10s+ tail latencies and some 504s. They're asking for repro steps and short-term mitigations.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled pool dp-42 8->16 at 09:15:45 UTC, queued=342 requests, avg-queue-ms=12000, p99-latency=11.2s

emily: Short-term mitigation idea: failover heavy requests to hosted-runner cluster or a lower-latency smaller model. Could also return 503+Retry-After for requests hitting extreme queue depth to avoid cascading backlog.

kevin: Implemented a temporary routing tweak: requests with max_tokens>1024 AND model in large-family are routed to fallback_pool for the next 30m. Also increased driver attach retries from 2->5.

james: Reproduced locally on a fresh node: initial GPU attach (nvml init + module load) can take 9-15s because modules compile or firmware loads. Our provisioning marks node READY before gpu-attach-ok flag which explains the observed warmup gap.

sandhya: Short-term operational options: 1) keep-warm N nodes per pool so we have buffer warm GPUs; 2) shrink scale step to avoid big simultaneous node additions; 3) increase parallelism for attach retries. Long-term: bake AMI with precompiled nvidia modules and firmware packaged.

maria: Oncall, please run keep-warm for dp-42 = 4 nodes until we fix images. Customers need reassurance.

kevin: Running command now: 
```
./rctl pool update dp-42 --keep-warm=4
# response: accepted request id=req-7844
```

maria: Support updated customers: "we've applied temporary mitigations (keep-warm + routing fallback). We're investigating and will follow up with RCA in 24h."

james: Follow-ups I'm adding to board: 1) create a pre-warmed AMI with precompiled nvidia kernel modules and firmware for all zones; 2) change provisioner to only mark node READY after gpu-attach-ok flag; 3) add autoscaler.warmup_ms metric and alert if >5000ms; 4) add per-zone image-sync verification job.

kevin: I'll spin up a small canary for the new AMI tonight and schedule a staged rollout if canary looks healthy. Also lowering autoscale step-size for dp-42 to reduce churn during next surge.

sandhya: FYI I found one more thing in /var/log/nvidia-init on a failed node: "missing firmware for xxx" — images in us-west-2 were missing a firmware blob after last image build. I'll open infra task to reconcile image sync across regions.

maria: Thanks. I'll assemble a one-pager for support and product (timeline, mitigations, action items). Please add any relevant logs & dashboards to the ticket. We'll close this thread once RCA doc is linked. :thumbsup:
